stances.claim: AIM's trifold posthumous honors -- Chapel rededication, caseroom naming, and a full scholarship -- appropriately recognize Prof. Leni Panganiban as the first female professor at AIM (MBM 1971), who taught for over three decades and served as Associate Dean for the MM Program, making her 'the first AIM faculty member to be conferred these honors.'

The Chapel of the Immaculate Conception was 'quietly and anonymously' built, adorned, and upgraded by Leni in partnership with Fr. James Donelan, SJ -- embodying the kind of devotion the marker memorializes (wisdom, inner strength, family love, lifelong Marian devotion).
stances.rhetorical_move: documented-virtue framing via reproduced marker text

stances.claim: The new AIM Master of International Business Law (MIBL) program -- which CJ proposed and which Dr. Jikyeong Kang accepted, with the curriculum designed over two years by professors Olivier Roche and Felipe Calderon -- is intended for non-legal-career professionals who want law to 'round out their business thinking,' modeled on Northwestern's MSBL where CJ's grandson Mig Sandejas earned his degree.
The MIBL is explicitly a business degree, NOT a law degree -- graduates 'cannot take the bar exam, much less practice law' -- locating it cleanly within AIM's business-education mission.

Since the MIBL 'promotes the safeguarding of liberty and the nurturing of prosperity under the rule of law,' FLP-MPIF will grant 2-3 fellowships of P450,000 each to first-batch enrollees -- operationalizing the twin-beacon philosophy at the program level.

AIM's framing of MIBL as 'interdisciplinary' (finance, leadership, risk management, HR, data analytics, information security in addition to law) makes it appropriate for diverse non-legal backgrounds aiming to 'thrive in the global business environment.'

one_paragraph_summary: On what would have been her 84th birthday -- Feb. 29, 2024 -- the Asian Institute of Management posthumously honored Prof. Leni Panganiban with a trifold tribute: rededicating the Chapel of the Immaculate Conception in her loving memory, naming a ground-floor caseroom after her, and opening the Professor Leni Panganiban Scholarship to be granted starting 2025 to an outstanding iMBA student. Born on a leap year (Feb. 29, 1940) and 'ascended to the Heavenly Kingdom aptly last Easter Sunday, April 9, 2023,' Leni is the first AIM faculty member to be conferred these honors. Presided over by AIM president and dean Dr. Jikyeong Kang, the 'simple but elegant and formal' Dedication Ceremony unveiled two commemorative markers Panganiban reproduces in full: the chapel marker honors Leni's partnership with Fr. James Donelan, SJ (AIM's first chaplain) in 'quietly and anonymously building, adorning, and upgrading this Chapel,' memorializing her 'wisdom, inner strength of character, enduring love for family, and lifelong devotion to our Risen Lord Jesus and to the Immaculate Conception of Our Lady'; the caseroom marker -- signed by CJ and the children Maria Elena, Jose Artemio III, Celine Maria, Maria Theresa, and Maria Evelyn -- recognizes her as the first female professor at AIM (MBM 1971), with over three decades of faithful teaching and service as Associate Dean for the MM Program. In appreciation, CJ and his children gave a modest donation to the AIM Scientific Research Foundation. He then pivots to a related institutional development: a few years ago CJ proposed to AIM a new Master of International Business Law (MIBL) program, inspired by his grandson Jose Miguel 'Mig' Sandejas, who after his Babson College MBA earned a Northwestern University Master of Science in Business Law without a basic law degree, writing CJ that 'knowledge of the law rounded out my business thinking ... The law helps guide the numbers and provides another solution for optimizing income, reducing expenses, and protecting shareholders.' Dr. Kang accepted the proposal and tasked a faculty team headed by professors Olivier Roche and Felipe Calderon to design the two-year-developed curriculum suitable for AIM's local and international milieu. Enrollment for the first batch closes March 15; the MIBL is explicitly a business degree, not a law degree, so graduates 'cannot take the bar exam, much less practice law.' Because the MIBL 'promotes the safeguarding of liberty and the nurturing of prosperity under the rule of law,' the Foundation for Liberty and Prosperity, in partnership with the Metro Pacific Investments Foundation, will grant at least two -- perhaps three -- P450,000 fellowships to first-batch enrollees. AIM's own framing positions MIBL as an interdisciplinary program (finance, leadership, risk management, HR, data analytics, information security alongside law) for non-legal-career professionals seeking to 'thrive in the global business environment.'
